# @ic-reactor/cli

> The `ic-reactor` command: generates typed declarations, a reactor with bound
> React hooks, and optionally one query or mutation object per method, from
> `.did` files. For projects without Vite, CI, and explicit generation runs.

Applies to `@ic-reactor/cli` 0.14.0.

Read this file from `node_modules/@ic-reactor/cli/llms.txt` when writing code
against the installed version. The complete guide for every package is
https://ic-reactor.b3pay.net/llms-full.txt, and behaviour changes are in
https://github.com/B3Pay/ic-reactor/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add -D @ic-reactor/cli
pnpm add @ic-reactor/react @icp-sdk/core @tanstack/react-query
pnpm exec ic-reactor init       # writes ic-reactor.json (and src/clients.ts)
pnpm exec ic-reactor generate   # run again after every .did change
```

Needs Node.js 22.12 or later, and TypeScript 5.7 or later in the app.

## Setup and Usage

`ic-reactor.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/@ic-reactor/cli/schema.json",
  "outDir": "src/declarations",
  "clientManagerPath": "../../clients",
  "canisters": {
    "backend": {
      "name": "backend",
      "didFile": "./backend/backend.did",
      "canisterId": "rrkah-fqaaa-aaaaa-aaaaq-cai",
      "factories": true
    }
  }
}
```

`src/clients.ts`, the module `clientManagerPath` points at from the generated
files:

```ts
import {
  AuthenticationManager,
  ClientManager,
  createAuthHooks,
  reactorRetry,
} from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { QueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query"

export const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: reactorRetry } },
})
export const clientManager = new ClientManager({ queryClient })

// Optional Internet Identity sign-in (needs @icp-sdk/auth); every generated
// reactor on this clientManager then calls as the signed-in user
export const authentication = new AuthenticationManager({ clientManager })
export const { useAuth, useUserPrincipal } = createAuthHooks(authentication)
```

`ic-reactor init` writes a plainer `src/clients.ts` (a `QueryClient` with
TanStack's defaults and the `ClientManager`); extend it as above.

Using the output of `generate`:

```tsx
import { getPostQuery, likePostMutation } from "./declarations/backend"

export function Post({ id }: { id: string }) {
  const { data: post } = getPostQuery([id]).useQuery()
  const like = likePostMutation.useMutation({
    invalidateQueries: [getPostQuery],
  })
  return <button onClick={() => like.mutate([id])}>{post?.likes} likes</button>
}
// Outside React: await getPostQuery([id]).fetch(), await likePostMutation.execute([id])
```

## When to Use What

| Need                                            | Use                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| A Vite app with watch-mode regeneration         | `@ic-reactor/vite-plugin` instead            |
| Any other project, or generation in CI          | `ic-reactor generate`                        |
| One canister only                               | `ic-reactor generate --canister <name>`      |
| Remove output of canisters no longer configured | `ic-reactor generate --clean`                |
| Only the `declarations/` files                  | `ic-reactor generate --bindgen-only`         |
| Query and mutation objects per method           | `"factories": true` on the canister          |
| No React in the app                             | `"target": "core"` (typed reactor, no hooks) |
| Raw Candid values instead of display values     | `"mode": "Reactor"`                          |

## Configuration

- Top level: `outDir` (required), `clientManagerPath` (default
  `../../clients`), `target` (`react` or `core`), `canisters` (required).
- Per canister: `name` and `didFile` (required), `outDir`,
  `clientManagerPath`, `target`, `mode` (`DisplayReactor` by default,
  `Reactor`, `CandidReactor`, `CandidDisplayReactor`,
  `MetadataDisplayReactor`), `canisterId`, `factories`.
- Set `canisterId` for any build not served from a local replica. Without it
  the generated reactor reads its id from the `ic_env` cookie, which a
  `ClientManager` trusts only on a local replica (or with
  `allowEnvConfig: true`), so importing it throws
  `canisterId is required for "backend"` in Node, during SSR and on a
  deployed origin.
- The config is validated before anything is written: a bad value fails with
  the file and field named. Each canister needs its own `outDir`.
- `init -y` never asks and keeps an existing `ic-reactor.json`; `init` writes
  only to the current directory.

## Generated Output

Per canister, under `<outDir>/<name>/`:

- `declarations/`: `idlFactory` (`.js`), `_SERVICE` (`.d.ts`) and a copy of
  the `.did`, named after the `.did` file;
- `index.generated.ts` (rewritten every run): `<name>Reactor` and, with
  `target: "react"`, six hooks `use<Name>Query`, `use<Name>SuspenseQuery`,
  `use<Name>InfiniteQuery`, `use<Name>SuspenseInfiniteQuery`,
  `use<Name>Mutation`, `use<Name>Method`;
- `index.factories.generated.ts` (with `factories: true`): `createQuery` or
  `createQueryFactory` as `<method>Query` for query methods, `createMutation`
  as `<method>Mutation` for update and oneway methods, in camelCase;
- `index.ts` (created once, yours): re-exports the managed files. An edited
  `index.ts` gets a printed warning until it has
  `export * from "./index.factories.generated"`.

`generate --clean` removes only directories that carry codegen's header and
belong to no configured canister, and is ignored with `--canister`.

## Do Not

- Edit `index.generated.ts`, `index.factories.generated.ts` or
  `declarations/`; change the `.did` or `ic-reactor.json` and generate again.
- Hand-write per-method `createQuery` / `createMutation` modules; set
  `factories: true`, and override one by exporting the same name from
  `index.ts`.
- Leave `canisterId` out for a production build.
- Import the generated modules into a React Server Component or build them
  per request: they are module scope and import hooks.
